context: Establish which published identifier fields have a named consumer before choosing a remedy. Prefer removing unread fields over salting them; salt only what a named consumer needs. Whatever is chosen must preserve the #1512 fixed point, so a stored corpus is never re-pseudonymized in place. This decision must be made before #1537 merges: fixing it afterwards costs a second full result_id rotation, and today the rotation is free.
description: machine_id_salt defaults to None, so the public pseudonym digest is computed over an empty salt, and the algorithm is documented. That makes every published pseudonym an offline confirmation oracle: a candidate value can be hashed and matched against the corpus with certainty, no false positives. A one-second dictionary sweep of 1550 candidates over the 1615 pseudonym occurrences in results-data confirmed two distinct tokens, and the double-hashed form of one of them is present on the public published-results branch, so double hashing provides no protection. The corpus privacy gate cannot see this: find_public_path_leaks detects plaintext only, so it reports the corpus clean while the corpus is recoverable by dictionary. Separately, machine_id appears nowhere in _project/scripts/ or results-explorer/src/ and the read model has no machine or host column, so the grouping these pseudonyms exist to support is not implemented; and none of working_dir, driver_runtime_python_executable, submission_path, database_path or engine_host is named as a published field in the hosted results contract. Not publishing a field dominates salting it. Do not record recovered plaintext values in this item, a commit message, or a PR body - _project/todo-db-export is committed to the repository, so this text is public. Tokens only.

work_units.evidence: Consumer audit across the pipeline (_project/scripts/explorer_pipeline, explorer_publish.py), the Explorer app (results-explorer/src), and the published contract (docs/reference/hosted-results-contract.md), for the 9 pseudonymised field names present in the corpus. Six have NO consumer in any of the three: machine_id, working_dir, driver_runtime_python_executable, database_path, data_path, engine_host. They account for roughly 1320 of the 1615 pseudonym occurrences. Three do: submission_path (contract only), database_name (Explorer app), endpoint (pipeline, app, and contract). The read model has no machine or host column at all, so the grouping these pseudonyms were introduced to protect - the stated motivation for #1512 - is not implemented anywhere. Confirms the reframe: for the six, not publishing dominates salting, because a pseudonym with no reader is pure liability and the transform is a public confirmation oracle.
work_units.summary: Establish which published identifier fields have a named consumer, first-party or contractual

work_units.evidence: Recorded as docs/development/adr/adr-published-identifier-field-set.md, Accepted. Decision: do not publish the six identifier fields with no consumer (machine_id, working_dir, driver_runtime_python_executable, database_path, data_path, engine_host); remove them at the publication boundary rather than pseudonymising them. Keep publishing pseudonyms for the three with readers (endpoint, database_name, submission_path) and leave the salt question open for those. Alternatives recorded with reasons: minting a default salt (rejected as primary - does not close the oracle for already-published bytes and keeps paying a privacy cost for data nothing reads; still right for the three with readers), and accepting the oracle (rejected - the exposure scales with contributors, and choosing to publish confirmable identifiers on their behalf is not ours to make silently). The ADR states the id-rotation consequence explicitly and that this supersedes #1537's field set so ids rotate once, not twice.
